{{pagebanner|Lviv banner 1.jpg|unesco=yes|unesco_cc=yes}}

'''Lviv''' (also spelled ''L'viv''; Ukrainian: Львів; Polish: ''Lwów'', German: ''Lemberg'', Russian: Львов), formerly known as '''Lvov''' after its Russian name, is in [[Western Ukraine]]. It's the biggest city of the region and a major Ukrainian cultural centre on the [[UNESCO World Heritage List]].  Visiting Lviv is very rewarding for the pioneer traveller, as living is extremely cheap here and the place has a truly authentic feeling, unlike places like Kraków or Prague, which are swamped with tourists.

=== History ===
[[File:Lwów - Cerkiew Uspieńska.jpg|thumb|Dormition Church and the 400-year-old Korniakt Tower]]
The city has a multicultural history but little of the evidence of this has survived until today. It was founded in 1256 by King Daniel of Galicia (Ukrainian: Король Данило Галицький - Korol' Danylo Halytskyy) and fell under Polish control in the 14th century. Poles, Jews, Ukrainians, Armenians, Germans and others lived there together for centuries. This multicultural experience virtually came to an end during and after WWII. Germans killed most of the Jews (about one third of Lviv's population at that time). At the end and in the direct aftermath of the war, the remaining Polish population (about 65% of the population) was then "repatriated" to Poland in its new borders by the Soviet government. Some Polish and Jewish heritage is preserved, for example remains of some synagogues and a number of catholic churches, also  one can find some inscriptions on former shops in Polish, Yiddish and German.

Because of Lviv's proximity to the EU and its openness to foreigners, the city's multicultural feel has experienced a resurgence. Even today, walking through the city centre, a traveller can hear Poles laughing and taking pictures of the beautiful old buildings, Germans walking through the city on guided tours, Ukrainian or Russian tourists and students joking about this or that, and American or British businessmen chatting in cafes. There is even a small Jewish community in the city. The many universities in Lviv attract students from every continent on the globe, and its old architecture draws tourists from various parts of the world, including Ukraine.

The Polish king John II Casimir founded the Lviv University in the 17th century and Lviv (known as ''Lwów'') was by that time one of the most important cities in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, along with [[Kraków]], [[Warsaw]], [[Gdańsk]] and [[Vilnius]].

In 1772 the city was taken by the Habsburgs, and in Austrian times it was known as ''Lemberg'', the capital of Galicia. After the dissolution of the Austro-Hungarian Empire in 1918, it was returned to Poland.

As a result of World War II, Stalin moved the Soviet frontier westward so Lviv became part of the USSR under its Russian name ''Lvov'' (still widely used by supporters of Russia, but very offensive to most locals). After Ukrainian independence in 1991, the Ukrainian name of ''Lviv'' was gradually adopted in English.

=== Identity ===
Lviv is the region of Ukraine with the strongest sense of Ukrainian identity. Even when it was part of the Soviet Union, most signs were only in Ukrainian, and only a few also in Russian. Because of its history as part of the [[Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]] and the [[Austro-Hungarian Empire]], Lviv has a Central European flair in its architecture that makes it one of the most beautiful cities in Eastern Europe, and also has a Catholic majority, unlike most of majority-Eastern-Orthodox Ukraine. Lviv has even been called "the capital of Ukrainian culture". The people there are very warm, although somewhat direct (which is very common in eastern Slavic cultures).

=== Tourism ===
The city is tourist-friendly. All downtown street signs are in Ukrainian and English, and the staff of the Information Center on Rynok Square speak many different languages. Maps, schedules of local events, and tourist guides can be obtained there for free in English, German, Polish, and Russian. There are small information kiosks beside some monuments (small touch-screen TVs that offer maps and information about the city).
* [https://lviv.travel/en lviv.travel Lviv Tourism] website.

The closest operating airports are in [[Poland]]. From the airport, take a train or a bus to Lviv, that will bring you into Ukraine across the border. 
* Jasionka International Airport {{IATA|RZE}} is a 4-hour train trip to Lviv.
* Krakow Airport {{IATA|KRK}} is a 6-hour train trip to Lviv.
* Lublin Airport {{IATA|LUZ}} is an 8-hour train trip to Lviv.
* Warsaw Airport {{IATA|WAW}} is a 10-hour train trip to Lviv.

===By car===
{{seealso|Western_Ukraine#By_car}}

From Poland: take the E40, this will end at the city centre. Formalities at the border take at least one hour. There will be a long line for trucks, which you can pass if you travel by car. Don't expect the border police to treat you respectfully, or speak any language other than Ukrainian, Polish or Russian. 

It is illegal to drive in the city centre (including Prospekt Svobody) on Sundays and holidays. This is signposted in Cyrillic only, and there are always police present to catch some unsuspecting foreigner.

=== By public transport ===
Single ride tickets in trams, trolleybuses, buses and marshrutka cost:

* 26 ₴, tap the validator inside the bus with NFC-enabled bank card or smartphone (Apple Pay or Google Pay).
* 23 ₴ if tapped with a [https://leocard.lviv.ua/ public transport card] LeoCard or [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.lvivavtodor.eticket app].
* 30 ₴ if paid in cash to the driver.

Lviv has a convenient public transport system that includes:

* 8 tram routes
* 10 trolleybus routes
* 18 bus routes
* 31 marshrutka routes

Monthly [https://tickets.lvivelectrotrans.com.ua/en travel passes]{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} are available for 420 ₴.

Passes can be used in trams and trolleybuses.

Schedules are available on [https://lad.lviv.ua the map] and on [https://lviv.rozklad.in.ua rozklad.in.ua] (in Ukrainian).

You can also check information about public transport on [https://city.dozor.tech/ua/lviv/city DozoR] (in Ukrainian), [https://www.eway.in.ua/en/cities/lviv EasyWay] and Google Maps.

=== By taxi ===
Taxi is the easiest way of getting around the city, and are very cheap by European standards. Most trips which are not of exceptional distance or at exceptionally busy times should cost under €5. Some popular taxi companies include:

* [https://www.uber.com '''Uber'''] (Убер)
* [https://bolt.eu '''Bolt'''] (Болт)
* [https://uklon.com.ua/en/ '''Uklon'''] (Уклон)
* [https://ontaxi.com.ua/en '''OnTaxi'''] (ОнТаксі)
* [https://opti.global/en/ '''Opti'''] (Опті)
* [https://shark-taxi.ua/en '''Shark'''] (Шарк)
* '''[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mobox.taxi&hl=uk&pli=1 Taxi838]''' 
Note: Many taxi apps do not operate during the 00:00-05:00 curfew. Uklon and Taxi838 are exceptions, and can be used to get to or from your hotel if your train departs or arrives during curfew.

Renting a kick scooter is a fun way to get around the city quickly.

Centre accented balcony on stone consoles, 18th century. Today the building is used as a dwelling house. Also there are more monument buildings on Krakivska str at numbers 4, 13, 15, 17 and 22.

| wikidata=Q4233747
| content=Built by order of Polish King Wladyslaw IV. Because it was the Main Royal Arsenal, built between the city walls. Completed in 1646. The façade of the building was decorated bronze sculptures, cast in 1639, now is in History Museum. The building is made of stone, rectangular plan, with two L-shaped wings connected by a wall, these walls to protect the east side of the patio. The façade decorated with balcony and pediment in baroque style. On the side façade of the east wing preserved carved stone portal in the Renaissance style.

* {{see
| name=Seasons house | alt=Кам'яниця Пори року | url= | email=
| address=Virmenska str., (Вірменська вул.) 23 | lat=49.84388 | long=24.03120 | directions=
| phone= | hours= | price=
| content=A plastered, elongated, four-storey house made of brick. The last renovation was in the 19th century, it holds its shape today. Façade design style of late classicism: the second and third floors are connected by Ionic pilasters, between them at the second floor is a depiction of Chronos and at the sides—four reliefs with scenes from people's everyday lives, symbolizing seasons. Above, in front stretched the entire length of frieze depicting the zodiac signs. Painted in 1860s. Also there monument houses on Virmenska street: No.&nbsp;17, 27 and 33.
}}
* {{see
| name=Domazhyrs'ka house | alt=Кам'яниця Домажирська | url= | email=
| address=Virmens'ka str., 15 | lat=49.84329 | long=24.03151 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=
| wikidata=Q84834556
| content=The house top floor made in the 18th century. A brick, plastered, three storey invalid rectangle form building with a narrow courtyard. The main architectural accent of the main facade is a big portal, keystone is the stone along with two symmetrically positioned consoles supporting a balcony with openwork metal grille.
}}
* {{see
| name=Ratusha (Town Hall) | alt=Ратуша | url= | email=
| address=Market Square, Ploshcha Rynok, Площа Ринок | lat=49.841835 | long=24.031326 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=
| wikidata=Q4271056
| content=You can climb the tower of the town hall: go in via the main entrance, wander about until you see a sign 'вхид на вежу', then follow those signs up 103 steps to a ticket-office and up 305 more steps to the top of the tower. There's a great view of the Old Town, and this is clearly one of the romantic spots of the city. The City Hall is made of brick, four-square plan, with patio, in 1830—1835, in the Viennese classicism style. Added the town hall a clock tower. Around the building on the square are three fountains in 1900s: first the Fountain Adonis (to Northeast) has a cup, which stands on the pavement, in the centre of a star, outlined in red and black stone. In the centre of the bowl—a statue of the hero character of ancient mythology Adonis with a dog and boar killed him; Fountain Neptune (to Southwest) In the centre of the bowl—a statue of ancient mythology character Neptune—the Roman god of freshwater and the sea—which is situated at the feet of dolphin; and also on the square is the Fountain Amphitrite (to Northwest) with a statue of ancient mythology character Amfitryta, consort of Neptune with a dolphin.
}}

Among the 150 000 copies - labours of theologians of Kyiv, Lviv, St. Petersburg and Moscow Theological Academies and their periodicals. And religious literature of Catholic institutions from Italy, Germany, Austria, France and Poland. A collection of religious books of the Crimean Khanate time, works of publishing house of Ukrainian Catholic University in Rome. A unique collection of Bibles in different languages: Greek, Latin, German, French, Chinese, English, etc. Among them—the Ostrog Bible of Ivan Fedorov, the Paris edition of 1563, and a Venetian edition of 16th century.

==Do==
[[File:LvivOperaHouse.JPG|thumb|right|320px|Lviv Opera House (Svobody Ave)]]

=== Culture ===
*Attend a '''concert or festival'''. Lviv has been called the "Queen of Festivals" as a city, because there is often a different festival every other week. Some festivals with many free activities are the Chocolate Festival, the Coffee Festival, and the Alpha Jazz Festival. Stop by the Tourist Information Center on Rynok Square to find out more about what festivals are happening during your stay in Lviv.
* {{do
| name=S. Krushelnytska Opera House | alt= | url=https://opera.lviv.ua/ | email=

| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=
| wikidata=Q1246092
| lastedit=2023-09-04
| content=In the very heart of Lviv the historic opera house offers regular performances of various operas and ballets. Tickets can be purchased at the theatre cashier ("Kaca") ranging in price from 50&nbsp;грн to 80&nbsp;грн. Even if opera and ballet is not your cup of tea, a night at the theatre is worthwhile, at the very least, to enjoy this spectacular venue.
}}

* Visit the '''Bania''', a Russian-style sauna for men and women (non-communal). There are a few in Lviv and well worth the trip. The experience can be mildly confronting for the prudish Westerner, as all activities are conducted in the nude but don't worry, it is a highly civilized environment.

===Money===
''For more information on currency see [[Ukraine#Money|here]]''

Apple Pay and Google Pay are commonly accepted in the restaurants, cafes, hotels and hostels. Also at the main bus station and long distance train station. All small grocery stores also accept bank card payments.

ATMs (known as "bankomats") and currency exchanges ("obmin valyuti") are ubiquitous throughout Lviv, particularly in the city center. Most ATMs will accept Visa and MasterCard. Currency exchanges will often only accept foreign currency in pristine condition, though this has changed since the beginning of the full-scale war (as demand for foreign currency has increased with the economic crisis).

Currency exchanges have locals, rather than foreigners, as their prime customers. It is very common for Ukrainians to keep their savings in USD or EUR, as they are seen as more stable means of storing value (there is a joke that one is not truly broke in Ukraine until one goes to sell their dollars). Therefore, to compete with each other for customers, currency exchanges offer very competitive, near-market rates for the most popular currencies, like USD, EUR, and PLN. 

Travellers' checks are not very useful in Lviv; however, there are still a few hotels and banks that will cash them for you.

Attempting to pay for something inexpensive in cash with a large denomination (200&nbsp;грн and above) will often at the very least annoy the shopkeeper; salespeople may even refuse to sell to you if you do not have any smaller denominations. Grocery stores and other high-volume shops are an exception to this rule.

* {{eat
| name=Pid Kelpsydroyu café/restaurant | alt=Under Clepsydra | url= | email=
| address=Vir’menska 35 | lat=49.8438 | long=24.0324 | directions=opp. Dzyga Cultural Centre, you'll see about 15 large tables with patio umbrellas crowding the street
| phone= | hours= | price=
| lastedit=2023-09-28
| content=You'll also see the city's sophisticated set sipping Under Clepsydra's famous forest tea. Under Clepsydra has three sections. The indoor café/restaurant inspired by the Parisian brasseries of the left bank has two sections, smoking and non-smoking, that share a soundtrack of classic French jazz and folk music. Upstairs you’ll find the more popular late-night section of the establishment. But what really sets it apart from other Lviv hangouts is the menu. Vegetarian restaurants in Lviv are, well, non-existent, but Under Clepsydra you’ll find a collection of fresh, meat-free dishes made with local ingredients. Potato and mushroom crepes are less than 80 грн, and fresh soups and salads are anywhere between 40-80 грн. Menus are in English. The carnivorous set has plenty of options as well. Few dishes run more than 200 грн, and entrees include duck, pork, grilled chicken, smoked salmon.
}}
* '''Boykivska Hostynya,'''  Mytropolyta Andreya St, 8: Located a bit outside of downtown near the St. Yuriy Cathedral complex and Lviv Polytechnic University, this restaurant is a tribute to the cuisine and culture of the Boyko people, a sub-ethnicity native to the nearby Carpathian Mountains. The owner, Andriy, runs a local non-profit for the promotion and preservation of Boyko culture.

==Drink==
Ukraine in general (and Lviv in particular) have developed a fantastic beer and wine scene since the Revolution of Dignity in 2014. In addition to mass-market brands like Chernihivske and Lvivske (which has its brewery in Lviv at Kleparivska 18 and includes a lovely beer museum), there is a wide variety of craft brands. Highlights include Pravda (an iconic Lviv brand with excellent beer and legendary bottle art, with its flagship location at the bottom of Ploscha Rynok), Mova, Ten Men, Varvar, Tsypa, and First Dnipro.  

Cheap beer on tap in Lviv is in the range of 60-80 UAH (~1.25-2.00 EUR). Crafty, expensive beer is in the 120-160 UAH (3-5 EUR) price range.

===Bars===
* '''Tsehla Bar''' (''Brick Bar in Ukrainian''), Brativ Rohatyntsiv, 9. This bar is the favorite hangout of the foreign volunteer crowd, particularly after volunteering shifts end at around 8 or 9 PM. Provides a standard offering of beers on tap, along with ciders, mixed drinks, and house-made liqueurs, all for low prices even by Lviv standards.
* '''Dobryy Druh Pub''' (Good Friend Pub), several locations across downtown. Dobryy Druh has around 5 pubs in the downtown area with standard and craft beers, cocktails, liqueurs, and standard pub food. Popular with younger crowds (especially the location on Kryva Lypa near Ivan Franko University), and often a good place to catch a football match.
* {{drink
| name=Kriyivka Bar | alt=Hiding Place in Ukrainian | url=https://www.fest.lviv.ua/uk/restaurants/kryjivka/ | email=
| address= | lat=49.841296 | long=24.032269 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=
| wikidata=Q12114941
| lastedit=2025-03-12
| content=“Slava Ukrayini” - the phrase means ‘Glory to Ukraine,’ and it’s your ticket to this underground, unmarked bar called Kryivka. When you do finally find it, state the password to a man toting a prop vintage machine gun, receive your shot of medovukha, and descend into the cozy wooden dining room you’ll be glad you took the time to find. This Ukrainian Independence themed bar is decorated with artifacts from Ukraine’s valiant struggle to stay autonomous - with guns, maps and posters lining the walls. You’ll also notice the names of dishes on the English menu harken back to a military tradition stretching back to the Austrian Empire. Culinary highlights include a half-metre long sausage, pickles soaked in honey and savory vereniky. There is also a bit of theatre during a dinner at Kryivka. If you’re lucky, a “Russian spy” may have snuck in to the restaurant and the brave staff will turn off the lights, grab a flashlight, root out this spy and serve him a healthy portion of justice. Once the intruder has been detached, celebratory live music erupts in the basement venue and locals burst into traditional songs of freedom. Kryivka on its peak popularity in early 2000s used to be an iconic bar and restaurant symbolizing Ukrainian Lviv patriotic history.
}}
* {{drink
| name=Hasova Lyampa Bar | alt=Kerosene Lamp | url=http://gasovalampa.lviv.ua/ | email=
| address=Virmenska 20 | lat= | long= | directions=
| phone=
| hours= | price=
| content=You’ll most likely see a man dressed in old time regalia pacing in front of the entrance, beckoning people inside. If he’s not there another greeter awaits in the form of a metal statue sitting at a desk with a... you guessed it, lit gas lamp. Once inside you’ll find a spiral staircase ascending up three flights of dining space. Each floor is cozy, candle lit, and decorated with classic gas lamps. Gas Lamp also has one of Lviv’s best patios, in the form of their rooftop dining section. While the entrees are standard, the snacks that go with beer are real standouts. Try the seasoned croutons, chips and a variety of dipping sauces they’re the perfect accompaniment for their wide selection of cold local brews.
}}

* {{drink
| name=Korzo Irish Pub | alt= | url= | email=
| address=Brativ Rohatinskiv street | lat= | long= | directions= off the main Rynok
| phone=
| hours= | price=
| content=Though it may sometimes seem like it, not every bar or restaurant in Lviv has some kind of theme or hook, and Korzo Pub is one of these places - nothing too fancy here, just an oak bar, brass taps and well worn tables that have eavesdropped on hundreds of conversations, arguments and romantic encounters. Korzo also has a great selection of international spirits, so if you’re the kind of person who needs a shot of tequila to get the night going, this is your place. As the beer flows, you might want to try the fish soup, hearty and robust, locals say it is the perfect ballast to prevent a hangover the next morning. If quenching your thirst on a sunny afternoon of exploring is your goal, Korzo has one of Lviv’s largest patios.
}}
* '''Drunken Duck''' (П'янна Качка), Brativ Rohatyntsiv St, 45. Along with its sister bar, '''St. Christopher Craft Beer University''' (Львівський Університет Крафтового Пива ім. Св. Христофора) at Ivana Franka, 3, Drunken Duck is a craft pub offering a wide variety of draft and bottled craft beers from Ukraine's leading craft breweries, along with well-made standard pub fare. This bar is an excellent place to try some of the best of what the Ukrainian craft beer revolution has to offer. While it is pricey by Lviv standards, you can enjoy a half liter of excellent craft beer for a maximum of around €4.
* '''Vynolovy (Винолови),''' Brativ Rohatyntsiv, 22: Like Ukrainian beer, Ukrainian wine has undergone an amazing transformation since 2014, and can now hold its head high amongst any other European country's wine industry. Vynolovy is an excellent place to sample the highlights of Ukrainian wine, with bottles at both lower and higher price points (although 500 грн is the beginning of Ukraine's higher price point), and with bottles from all over the country. The staff speaks decent English and is knowledgeable and proud of their products. 
* '''More Vina (Море Вина),''' Dzhokhar Dudaev St, 22: A hangout of the local intellectual sort which is a bit outside of the main downtown area, More Vina offers super cheap but rather good Ukrainian wine. Enjoy a full 250 ml glass for less than €1.50 while listening to soft music and admiring the paintings of local artists. 

===Clubs===
Ukraine's nightlife is constrained by the wartime curfew, but there is still fun to be had until everything shuts down by around 23:30.

* {{drink
| name=Club Metro disco | alt=Нічний клуб | url=http://metroclub.com.ua | email=
| address=Zelena 14 | lat= | long= | directions=outskirts of the centre
| phone=+380 32 2 42-07-88 | hours= | price=
| lastedit=2023-09-28
| content=Metro isn’t the easiest place to spot during the day, but at night, just follow the hordes of fabulously dressed young people as they make their way there. Entrance will probably set you back about 120 грн and once inside the first thing you’ll see is a large disco. A raised platform in the centre of the dance floor features male and female go-go dancers (and any brave customers who decide to join them on stage). A bar opposite provides local beers, vodka and champagne. For a change of pace, head downstairs where you’ll find two more bars. One serves the techno and house room, the other the lounge, private rooms and the hip hop dance floor. To cool off from all of the dancing, hit the giant upstairs patio with its heat lamps during winter and umbrellas for those rainy Lviv nights.
}}
* {{drink | name=Pozitiff | url=http://pozitiff.ae/ | email= | address=14 Zelena St. | lat= | long= | directions= | phone=+380 32 2 29-49-05 | hours= | price= | lastedit=2023-09-28 | content=If you’ve been to Metro Club you may have noticed a long line of locals trying to gain access to Pozitiff. This place is not easy to get into, and there are no guarantees that your money, passport or even begging can ensure you gain entrance. It’s all the bouncers call. Your best bet is to arrive with a small group of the most attractive people you can find. At this point the door man will either let you in, or not. If he does you’ll have negotiate an entrance fee. This cover charge usually depends on how cool and attractive your group is: The better-looking, the lower the fee. Expect to pay close to 240 грн for entrance. As entrance is so difficult, some patrons make the most of their trial, floating through the bar mingling, chatting and flirting. Others, displaying the icy confidence that got them in in the first place simply recline in their booth and radiate cool. No matter how you choose to play this one you’ll find enough friendly professionals to chat with and if you need to check your email, the Internet café section remains operational even into the wee hours of a rocking party.
}} {{Dead link|date=October 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}

==Sleep==
Lviv has a variety of hotels, hostels and apartments to suit all budgets and needs. The best deals for budget travellers (2-3 people) are found with the lovely apartments for rent all over town. These can be found online (preferably in Russian) or on arrival at the train station. Expect to pay 6,000-8,000 грн/month for a nice studio apartment with a kitchen, TV and a nice warm-water bathroom.

==Connect==
The dialing code for Lviv is +380 32(2). The telephone system has been modified; thus, to dial 6-digit numbers, use the city prefix 322, but for 7-digit numbers, use only 32.

All calls to and from cell phones are treated as long distance calls. The telephone system was modified one more time, thus, you must not dial an 8 followed by the city/mobile prefix, followed by the phone number. Some frequent mobile prefixes are 050, 066, 067, 071, 073, 095, 096, 097 and 099. The main mobile operators are Kyivstar, Vodafone, and Lifecell. You can buy a SIM card or a balance replenishment card at many stores throughout Lviv.

Mobile internet on Ukrainian SIMs is very cheap by European standards. A monthly plan with all the data you need (20+ GB) costs €5-6 (as of 2025).

Almost all restaurants and cafes provide free Wi-Fi, staff will typically provide a password on request.

==Stay safe==
Wartime dangers in Lviv are low. It is quite rare that drones or missiles actually attack the city (2-3 times per year, compared to nearly nightly raids against Kyiv), but it has happened before, tragically killing innocent people. 

To be notified of air raids and the type of possible incoming threat, download the Повитряна Тривога (Air Raid Alert) app ([https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ukrainealarm&hl=en Google Play], [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/%D0%BF%D0%BE%D0%B2%D1%96%D1%82%D1%80%D1%8F%D0%BD%D0%B0-%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%B2%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%B0/id1611955391 Apple]) and set the location to wherever you are in the country. It has full English functionality and is voiced by Mark Hammill (who will sternly remind you to take shelter when an air raid is announced and assure you when the all-clear is given). The app also announces when drones or missiles are flying in your general area.

If there is an air raid siren during the day in Lviv, it will almost certainly pass uneventfully (they are ordered across the country every time a certain type of Russian warplane starts flying). If a siren sounds during the night, a cautious person may wish to relocate to their hotel's basement or to remain in an area between two solid walls like a corridor or bathroom. If you decide to travel to Kyiv and cities further east, the air raid dangers increase significantly, and your safety protocols should be more strict.

Petty crime is low in comparison to much of the rest of Europe, and it is generally easy to stay safe by exercising common sense, not getting too drunk, and being a civil and polite person. That said, be mindful of pretty women at bars who seem a bit too friendly and watch your pockets in heavily-trafficked areas.

It is wise for men in particular to keep their passports or other proof that they are foreigners with them at all times during the war. Conscription officers (known locally as ТЦК/TeTseKa) sometimes patrol the cities (particularly the train station) and stop men to inspect their draft cards and even take them to the military. You will not be conscripted as a foreigner, but being able to prove that you are not Ukrainian will ensure that your interaction with these officers ends quickly. 

===Curfew===
To maintain wartime security, there is a curfew every day from 00:00 until 05:00. It is not very strictly enforced in Lviv, but you can expect the streets to be basically empty during those times. If you find yourself on the street during curfew, it is best to make your way home. If you are stopped by police or other security forces, show them your documents, tell them you are on your way home, and then go home.

Uber does not operate during curfew, but apps like Uklon and Taxi838 do. 

==Cope==
It can be very helpful to learn some [[Ukrainian]] before visiting, or at least the Cyrillic alphabet. Foreigners will be forgiven for speaking Russian (many internally displaced people from the eastern regions living in the city still do), but Leopolitans take language quite seriously. Many shops and restaurants will have signs on their doors specifically indicating that they will not speak Russian. The war has intensified feelings of loyalty to the Ukrainian language, and many people feel strongly about it.

That said, tourist-facing businesses will most often have English-speaking staff, and tours are available in many languages. Guests who speak Polish will find Lviv relatively easy to navigate, as the Lviv dialect of Ukrainian is especially close to Polish. 

In comparison to other cities in Ukraine, Lviv is lightly touched by the ongoing war. That said, the war touches everything and everyone. The city is home to a large number of internally displaced people, and many people have friends or family who either live under Russian occupation or have been injured or killed by Russian aggression. Every morning at 09:00, the country observes a minute of silence in which traffic stops and people pause to honor the fallen. On most mornings as of 2025, there is a funeral procession which travels down Prospekt Svobody (the main drag in the center) carrying a fallen soldier to their final resting place. Do not gawk or patronize. Be respectful of what Ukraine and its people are enduring in order to keep their country.

==Go next==
* [[Kyiv]]
* [[Odesa]]
* [[Bukovel]]. Millions visit Bukovel in the Carpathian Mountains every year. You may take a train to Bukovel, it's a great town to explore the Ukrainian nature and do some hiking / skiing depending on a season.
* [[Lutsk]]
* [[Rivne]]
* [[Transylvania]], [[Romania]]: To go south, take a bus to [[Chernivtsi]] (a bumpy 6½- hour ride, or you can take one of overnight trains). Near Chernivtsi, you can visit the lovely [[Kamianets-Podilskyi]] with its ancient castle. The bus to [[Suceava]] takes around 4 hours with border formalities. The buses from Suceava to [[Bacau]] and finally to [[Braşov]] take about 4 hours apiece on very bumpy roads.
